subject: Human Evolution
title: Taphonomy: How Fossils Form
description: Learn Taphonomy: How Fossils Form in one minute.

hook.text: For every fossil we find, millions of individuals rotted away without a trace. Fossilization is incredibly rare.

buildup.text: A body must be buried quickly—by sediment, ash, or water—before scavengers and bacteria destroy it.

discovery.text: Minerals slowly replace bone over millennia, turning organic tissue into stone through permineralization.

twist.text: Taphonomy—the study of how things fossilize—tells us as much about bias in the record as about the past.

climax.text: Forest-dwellers rarely fossilize because acidic soil dissolves bone. We may be missing entire lineages.

punchline.text: What we find is shaped by what survives.

quiz.question: Why are fossils of forest-dwelling species rare?
